verdict.instructions: Classify the mail. Check phishing/scam markers before promo/ham. Abstain when the mail carries no interpretable content.

criteria.ham: Personal or transactional mail — invoices, order confirmations, replies, direct human messages; no pressure or deception
criteria.promo: Legitimate bulk marketing or automated digest — unsubscribe link or recognizable brand, no deception
criteria.phishing: Asks for credentials/card/OTP, spoofs a known brand linking to an unrelated domain, or uses a password-protected archive
criteria.scam: Advance-fee/prize/lottery/investment fraud — money promised if the recipient pays or replies first

credential_risk.instructions: True only when the mail asks the recipient to enter or send credentials, card numbers, OTP, or ID documents. A wire/fee request does NOT count — that is scam, not credential risk.

spam_score.instructions: How unwanted the mail is for a typical recipient
criteria: Clearly wanted — transactional or human-written; 'order confirmation', 'your invoice', a direct reply; no pressure
Bulk or mildly suspicious — 'unsubscribe', '% off', automated digests, vague business outreach ('quick question, are you the right person?')

Clearly unwanted or dangerous — phishing, scam, threats, deceptive links, 'verify your account', 'you won', 'wire transfer'. Does NOT count: unsubscribe links or marketing language alone (that's level 1)
